questions.question: Which Scottish manager led Coventry City to Premier League survival for four consecutive seasons between 1997 and 2001, famously signing players like Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji?
questions.explanation: Gordon Strachan managed Coventry City from 1996 to 2001, keeping the Sky Blues in the top flight with remarkable escapes before their eventual relegation in 2001.
questions.anchorClues: Gordon Strachan / Coventry City Premier League

questions.question: True or False: Portsmouth are the only club in Premier League history to have been hit with a 9-point deduction for entering administration during a top-flight season.
questions.explanation: In March 2010, Portsmouth became the first Premier League club to enter administration, receiving an automatic 9-point deduction that sealed their relegation.

questions.question: What was the final scoreline when Tottenham Hotspur defeated Chelsea at White Hart Lane in November 2006, recording their first league win over Chelsea in 16 years?
questions.explanation: Aaron Lennon scored a memorable winner as Martin Jol's Spurs beat Jose Mourinho's Chelsea 2–1, ending a 32-game league winless run against their London rivals.

questions.question: Which historic ground served as the home stadium for Leicester City for 111 years before the club relocated to the King Power Stadium in 2002?
questions.explanation: Leicester City played at Filbert Street from 1891 until May 2002, closing the stadium with a 2–1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur.
questions.anchorClues: Filbert Street / Leicester City home stadium

questions.question: True or False: Everton have competed in every single Premier League season since the competition's formation in 1992 without ever suffering relegation.
questions.explanation: Everton are one of six clubs (alongside Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester United, and Tottenham Hotspur) to have maintained continuous Premier League status since 1992.
questions.anchorClues: Everton continuous Premier League status since 1992

questions.question: Which manager took charge of Fulham in December 2007 and pulled off a dramatic final-day survival before leading the West London side to the UEFA Europa League final two years later?
questions.explanation: Roy Hodgson orchestrated a remarkable comeback in the closing weeks of the 2007–08 season, culminating in a 1–0 win at Portsmouth on the final day to secure survival.
questions.anchorClues: Roy Hodgson / Fulham survival 2007–08 and Europa League

questions.question: Which squad number did Australian winger Harry Kewell wear during his five seasons at Liverpool between 2003 and 2008?
questions.explanation: Harry Kewell wore the number 7 shirt for Liverpool after signing from Leeds United in 2003, featuring in the 2005 UEFA Champions League victory in Istanbul.

questions.question: Which French winger won both the PFA Players' Player of the Year and FWA Footballer of the Year awards in 1998–99 while playing for Tottenham Hotspur?
questions.explanation: David Ginola enjoyed an outstanding 1998–99 campaign at White Hart Lane, becoming one of the few players to win both major individual awards in a season without winning the league title.
questions.anchorClues: David Ginola / PFA Player of the Year 1998–99 Tottenham

questions.question: Which English striker scored 18 Premier League goals for Coventry City during the 1997–98 season, finishing as joint-top scorer in the competition before joining Aston Villa?
questions.explanation: Dion Dublin shared the Premier League Golden Boot in 1997–98 with 18 goals for Coventry City before moving to Villa Park.
questions.anchorClues: Dion Dublin / Coventry City and Aston Villa

questions.question: Which Welsh forward holds the Premier League record for scoring for seven different clubs in the competition, netting for Coventry, Newcastle, Blackburn, Liverpool, West Ham, Manchester City, and Cardiff City?
questions.explanation: Craig Bellamy set the record by scoring for seven different Premier League clubs during an adventurous top-flight career spanning over 15 years.
questions.anchorClues: Craig Bellamy / Scored for 7 Premier League clubs record
